A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
colorectal carcinoma and lymphomas are not commonly found in the same patient, and that the lymphomas are usually of the non-Hodgkin's type.

the incidence of lymphoma in patients with colorectal carcinoma is low, that the lymphoma may be primary in the colon or rectum, or it may be a manifestation of lymphoma elsewhere in the gastrointestinal tract, that the lymphomas are of the B cell type, and that the prognosis is poor.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a lymphoma in patients with colorectal carcinoma does not necessarily imply a poor outcome.
the presence of a lymphoma in a patient with colorectal cancer should be regarded as a marker for a more aggressive form of the disease, with a worse prognosis.
colorectal carcinoma and lymphomas are not as uncommon as previously thought.
